vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lingxi-memory
Version: 1.1.1

The skill is designed to automatically scan, read, and exfiltrate OpenClaw session logs to external Feishu (Lark) documents and tables. While this is the stated purpose, the scripts (do_extract_and_write.sh and session_check.sh) contain hardcoded default Feishu IDs and tokens (e.g., ou_97d6f0bcc1bde8e3cc4f188ed574b3f, DdCMbcIrWawtlisBGwTcDEnznis), which would result in sensitive user conversation data being sent to the author's infrastructure by default. The system also uses crontab for persistence and background execution to monitor all session activity.

llm.summary: The skill implements the advertised session-extraction → Feishu write flow, but its manifest does not declare required credentials and the scripts contain hardcoded Feishu IDs/tokens/targets—this mismatch and embedded defaults could cause your sessions to be written to someone else's Feishu resources unless you carefully reconfigure it.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (read OpenClaw session files, extract memories, write to Feishu) matches what the scripts do. However the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or credentials while the SKILL.md and scripts clearly require Feishu configuration (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) and OpenClaw tooling. The absence of these required env declarations in the manifest is an incoherence that could mislead users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts read all OpenClaw session files under /root/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions, parse full conversation content, and invoke the OpenClaw agent/CLI to perform AI extraction and send writes/notifications to Feishu. That scope is consistent with the stated purpose, but the extraction prompt embedded in the script instructs the agent to call Feishu-writing tools with specific hardcoded app_token/table_id/doc_ids and to send notifications to a hardcoded user target. Embedding these IDs in the prompt grants the ability to send extracted conversation contents to those external Feishu endpoints (possibly not owned by the installer).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with two bash scripts to copy into your workspace; there is no package download or external installer. That lowers installation risk. The scripts are meant to be put under the user's workspace and scheduled via cron, so they will run on your host if installed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Although the registry lists no required environment variables, the SKILL.md and scripts depend on multiple Feishu-related env vars and an OpenClaw environment (.env, openclaw CLI). Additionally, the scripts contain hardcoded defaults and concrete-looking tokens/IDs (e.g., FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID default value, EXTRACT_PROMPT embeds L2 app_token DdCMbcIrWawtlisBGwTcDEnznis and table/doc IDs). Hardcoded identifiers/credentials increase the risk that extracted session contents will be delivered to external accounts without explicit consent. This is disproportionate and not declared in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills' configurations. Persistence is achieved by instructing users to install cron entries and copy scripts into the workspace; that is a normal deployment pattern for a scheduled job. Note: installing the cron job gives the skill ongoing access to local sessions and will repeatedly run until removed—ensure you understand and consent to that ongoing access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:

- Do not assume the manifest declares everything: the scripts expect Feishu credentials and OpenClaw tooling even though the registry lists none. Inspect and supply your own FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID in workspace/.env before running.
- The scripts include hardcoded defaults and concrete-looking Feishu tokens/IDs and a hardcoded notification target. Replace any hardcoded IDs/tokens with your own values or remove them. If you see tokens you don't recognize, do not run the scripts until you remove them.
- Understand data flow and privacy: the skill reads all local OpenClaw session files and will send extracted content to Feishu (cloud). Do not use this on conversations containing sensitive or regulated data unless you explicitly trust the configured Feishu destination and have appropriate consent/controls.
- Run scripts as a restricted user (avoid running as root) and review the cron entries you add. The scripts create files under your workspace and /tmp and will run periodically once scheduled.
- Verify openclaw CLI/agent behavior in a safe test environment first (sample session files) to confirm where data goes and what the agent writes. Monitor the Feishu targets to ensure content is written only to destinations you control.

Given the clear mismatches and hardcoded IDs, treat this skill as potentially risky until you replace defaults and confirm destinations; proceed only if you can inspect and control all Feishu credentials and targets.
